overall: The AG found three violations: the chair omitted the reconvene-in-open-session statement before a February 3, 2014 executive session; the February 10, 2014 notice failed to identify the non-union personnel; and general compensation policy was discussed in an improper executive session. Compliance was ordered and part of the minutes must be released.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the chair did not state, before the February 3, 2014 executive session, whether open session would reconvene afterward.
allegations.key_passage: while we find that the Committee's failure to make the required statement did violate the law, we are satisfied that the Committee is now aware of its obligations and has pledged to comply going forward.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the February 10, 2014 notice's executive session topic ('Non-Union Personnel') did not identify the specific personnel to be negotiated with.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee failed to identify in the notice for its February 10, 2014 meeting the specific non-union personnel with whom it intended to negotiate.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the February 10, 2014 executive session, claimed under Purpose 2 (nonunion negotiations), was used to discuss general compensation policy.
allegations.key_passage: we find that this portion of the meeting should not have occurred behind closed doors.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Publicly release at its next regularly scheduled meeting the portion of the February 10, 2014 executive session minutes concerning the discussion of compensation policy.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Committee that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law. Additionally, we order the Committee to publicly release at its next regularly scheduled meeting the portion of its February 10, 2014 executive session minutes concerning the discussion of compensation policy.
